clue.text: Simple cockney with no feelings

indicators.note: a cockney speaker drops the H, so the word for unfeeling is said the London way

parts.note: someone with no feelings is heartless, lacking compassion

explanation.surface: A simple-minded Londoner who feels nothing for anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the working-class accent of East London, drops initial H, so 'heartless' comes out as ''eartless', which sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple here means naive and guileless, without cunning or sophistication.

clue.text: Give permission for a very quiet range

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
to range is to wander or roam about

explanation.surface: Someone authorises a silent stretch of land or a shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: To give permission for something is to sanction or authorise it.

clue.text: Headdress for one in the seat of Irish kings

indicators.note: in says the letter for one is placed within the name of the royal seat

parts.note: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the ancient seat of the High Kings of Ireland
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A crown worn by a monarch sitting at an ancient Irish royal site.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular band worn on the head is a kind of headdress.

clue.text: Remove upset male in tie

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the following words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports report: the men's team is knocked out after a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is part of the anagram fodder, MALE IN TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove is to get rid of or knock out, as a team is knocked out of a tournament.

clue.text: Extinguish tobacco

definitions.meaning: to put out a candle flame by pinching it
powdered tobacco sniffed up the nose

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: putting out a candle, and powdered leaf inhaled through the nose.

clue.text: Overwhelm with papers after work

indicators.note: after says the newspapers come behind the work in the answer

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work of music
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Someone buried under paperwork once the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm people is to crush or burden them under harsh rule.

clue.text: Supervision an error

definitions.meaning: the job of watching over and managing
a mistake made by failing to notice something

explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers watching over work and failing to notice something, a slip or omission.

clue.text: Serving plate for some flour, say

indicators.note: serving here hints the letters of plate are dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dish used to serve out a portion of flour in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flour, say' is a pun on flower, and some of a flower is one of its coloured leaves; 'say' marks the flower as said aloud rather than spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured leaf forms one part of a bloom, so it is some of a flower.

clue.text: Walk along the seafront — and see lap dancing

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of the preceding words move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Stroll by the sea and watch lap dancing on the promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade beside the sea is a level public walk along the shore.

clue.text: Delay pay out across America

indicators.note: across says the word for paying out is laid over and around the short form for America

parts.note: to spend is to pay out money
US is the abbreviation for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A payment is held up while money is sent to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay something is to put it off or postpone it for a time.

clue.text: Paid, with no help — scope for a meaningless remark

indicators.note: with no means the word for help is taken away from the first word

parts.note: aid is help or assistance
latitude is scope or freedom of action

explanation.surface: Someone paid but given no assistance is offered freedom, and only empty words.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused saying offered as if wise is a meaningless remark.

clue.text: Records primate in empty theatres

indicators.note: in places the primate within what is left of the theatres
empty means the word theatres is cleared of its inside letters, leaving its first and last

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Accounts of a monkey loose in deserted playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Recordings made on magnetic strip are records of sound or video.

clue.text: All right! A holy animal

parts.note: OK means all right
pi is a slang short form of pious, meaning holy

explanation.surface: An exclamation of approval for a sacred creature.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for holy or sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe's striped forest relative from central Africa is an animal.

clue.text: One gets fired if all used together!

indicators.note: together here says the letters of the preceding words are mixed into one batch

explanation.surface: A worker warns that misusing everything at once means getting sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests losing a job; here it is guns being discharged, all shots at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst of many guns discharged at once is something that gets fired.

clue.text: English going mad and making an impression

parts.note: raving means going mad or acting wildly

explanation.surface: An Englishman losing his mind and creating a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making an impression' suggests influence; here it is literal, cutting a design into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a design into metal or wood leaves an impression, a print taken from the plate.

clue.text: Almost got around the poet — what's he wearing?

indicators.note: around says the cut-down word for got goes round the poet
almost means the last letter of the word for got is dropped

parts.note: gained means got or obtained
the Bard is Shakespeare, the poet

explanation.surface: Asking what the nearly dressed poet has on.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm twill cloth, or a raincoat made of it, is something a man might be wearing.

clue.text: Annoyed, having a change of heart, and opened channels

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for annoyed is swapped for another letter

parts.note: irritated means annoyed

explanation.surface: A cross farmer relents and lets water into the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the nine-letter word for annoyed is its fifth letter, T, which changes to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering land by digging ditches and channels to bring water to crops.

clue.text: Save nothing in difficult environment

indicators.note: in, with environment, says nothing sits inside the word for difficult

parts.note: hard means difficult
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Saving up nothing in a harsh economic climate.
explanation.definitionFit: To save things up in a secret stock is to stockpile them.

clue.text: A drop of the hard stuff

definitions.text: A drop of the hard stuff

parts.words: A drop of the hard stuff
parts.note: a drop of the hard stuff usually means a shot of spirits; read literally it is a frozen pellet falling from the sky

explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling from a cloud is a drop of something hard.

clue.text: The lead in television, for example

definitions.text: The lead in television, for example

parts.words: The lead in television, for example
parts.note: the lead in television sounds like the star of a show; read literally it is a wire carrying the signal into the set

explanation.definitionFit: A wire connecting a set to the signal is a lead, and cable TV is a form of delivery.

clue.text: 2k with first firm order

indicators.note: first says the abbreviation for firm comes at the front

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
2k means two thousand, and M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them
and means with, joining things

explanation.surface: A coded order: two thousand units, with the company given priority.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction given by someone in authority is an order.

clue.text: Keeps the monarch in servants

indicators.note: in places the monarch inside the word for keeps

parts.note: retains means keeps
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: The household keeps the queen among her servants.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Old family retainers are long-serving servants of a household.

clue.text: Salary? Mines up, terminal

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word for mines is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pits are mines
end means terminal or final point

explanation.surface: A miner's pay: the mines are closing for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular payment, as to a clergyman, is a salary.

clue.text: Loans arranged — go get arms!

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the following words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bank raid: loans are sorted, now fetch the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Money borrowed to buy a house, secured on the property, is a kind of loan.

clue.text: Some mogul agents found in the prison system

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some secret agents of a tycoon are sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'found in' into the definition; it is a link joining wordplay to 'the prison system', which alone swaps for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet network of forced-labour camps was a vast prison system.

clue.text: A prison officer's salary, commonly

definitions.meaning: in slang a jailer or warder
in informal British use, wages or pay

explanation.definitionFit: Slang supplies both: a warder in jail, and pay, as in earning a good wage.

clue.text: Fish found in the Caucasus hills

indicators.note: found in says the answer lies inside the run of letters across the following words

explanation.surface: A fish discovered in a mountain range between Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese raw fish with vinegared rice is a fish dish, loosely called fish.

clue.text: Hard up family in the outskirts of stockport

indicators.note: in places the family inside the letters left at the edges
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: kin are family

explanation.surface: A poor family living on the edge of a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockport is a town near Manchester in north-west England. SKINT is British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for broke, penniless, short of money.

clue.text: Swallow of the air, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for of the air is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: aerial means of or in the air

explanation.surface: A bird of the sky, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The fairy martin of Australia is Petrochelidon ariel, and Chambers lists the word as a kind of swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to an Australian bird of the martin family, a type of swallow.

clue.text: Mistake in links heard to cause fear

indicators.note: in places the mistake inside the spoken form of links
heard says the word for links is taken by its sound, then spelt another way

parts.note: ties are links or connections
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A golfer's blunder on the course, overheard, scaring everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' looks like a golf course; it means TIES, whose sound is respelt TISE (as in the -ise ending), with ERROR put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill people with terror is to cause fear among them.

clue.text: Cleared a channel for doctor border to start dispensing

parts.note: an edge is a border

indicators.note: to start says only the opening letter of dispensing is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor at the border opens a route for supplies of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape silt from a river bed to deepen it is to clear a channel.

clue.text: Taken by force, the others married outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for married goes round the others

parts.note: wed means married
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Everyone else was wed and carried off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seized or wrenched away from someone has been taken by force.
